resources.string: Messaging that answers to you — not to a company.
This takes a second. Everything happens on this device — nothing has been sent anywhere yet.
Onym runs on independent services for delivery, files and timestamps. Start with a set that works, or pick your own.
If someone reports illegal content, an authority you choose reviews the report. Pick one to continue — you\'ll see exactly what it can do before you agree.
These 12 words are the only way back into your account if you lose this device. Onym cannot reset them for you.
Your identity is on this device and your services are connected.
Your identity key is made on this device and stays here. No account, no phone number.
You pick who carries your messages — and can swap them any time in Settings.
You pick who handles reports, and see exactly what they can do before you agree.
12 words — you\'ll back these up in a moment
Your keys couldn\'t be created. Nothing was sent anywhere — try again.
Your key is the only thing that proves this account is yours. No server holds a copy of it.
Services published by Onym, verified on this device. Ready in a second.
Pick your own directories, relays, storage and notaries. About two minutes.
Whichever you choose, every service can be added, replaced or removed later in Settings.
Set up as much or as little as you like — anything you leave alone keeps the recommended default.
Carries photos, video and voice notes
More than one service works differently per category: relays all carry every message together, extra media hosts are trusted download sources, and each new group picks its notary from your list.
Anything you already added here stays configured — you can remove it later in Settings.

Relays pass sealed messages along. They can\'t read them, and they never learn who you\'re talking to. Every message is sent through all of your relays at once — any one of them is enough to reach you.
Every relay in this list carries every message — they\'re used together, not as fallbacks. Any one that\'s up is enough to reach you.
No relay configured yet. Add one below, or go back to keep the default.
Photos, video and voice notes are too big for the relays that carry text, so they travel through a media service instead. They\'re encrypted on this device first — it only ever handles sealed blobs.
Your uploads go through the active service only. Any others in the list are hosts you trust for downloading what people send you.
No server configured yet. Add one below, or go back to keep the default.
A directory is a phone book of available services. Onym verifies every entry on this device before showing it to you — adding a second one widens what you can choose from.
Already confirmed — its key is pinned.
No discovery provider is configured yet. Add your own below, or continue with the built-in defaults.
This build runs without a service directory. Continue — the app uses its built-in defaults.
Its catalogs are being fetched and verified now — the next steps can offer what it lists.
A notary keeps every group\'s membership and history honest. It checks each change with a zero-knowledge proof, so it can confirm a group is genuine without learning who is in it or what was said.
When you create a group, Onym picks one of these notaries at random for it — everyone in that group then uses the same one.
New groups are notarised by your primary notary.
No notary chosen yet. Pick one below, or leave this empty to use the published defaults.
Leave this empty to use the published defaults — they\'re installed automatically once setup finishes.
Reveal the 12 words, write them down, then verify a few of them. Takes about a minute.
You\'ve seen the 12 words. Verifying a few of them makes sure your copy is right.
You revealed and verified your phrase. Keep it somewhere safe — off screenshots and out of chats.
Anyone with these words can read your future messages. Keep them off screenshots and out of chats.
Everything here can be changed later in Settings. Nothing is permanent except your recovery phrase.
Your identity key was created on this device and exists nowhere else. Back it up from Settings → Back Up Keys so you can recover your account.
You\'ve seen the 12 words. Verify a few of them from Settings → Back Up Keys to make sure your copy is right.
